chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying:
“When you come to water and there are only a few people at it, then sprinkle to your right, to your left, and in front of you, and perform wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.قِلَّةٌ: a small number, referring here to there being few people present
key_terms.مَاءً: water used here as the source for ritual purification

ai.seo_question: What should one do before performing wudu (ablution) at a water source when only a few people are there?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical ruling related to wudu (ablution) at a water source when few people are present. It instructs sprinkling water around oneself before performing wudu (ablution), reflecting rulings and etiquette connected to ritual purity.
